bull_case: Management has repeatedly reinvested into low-cost distribution, underwriting, deposits and new countries, while the 2026 buyback deployed capital at a large discount to the frozen Base value.
bear_case: Founder voting control is very high, reducing minority-shareholder influence. Aggressive credit and international expansion can become value-destructive if strong current ROE proves cyclical.
thesis: Management allocation is strong with a governance discount. Nu repurchased 40.66M shares for $500.4M at about $12.31/share, only 66% of the frozen Base value. Execution across Brazil, Mexico and AI underwriting has been strong. Compensation is designed around long-term equity alignment. The principal weakness is founder control: David Vélez retains dominant voting power, which limits minority checks and prevents a higher governance score.

evidence.claim: Nu repurchased 40.6596M Class A shares for $500.393M by June 30, 2026, an average price of about $12.31/share versus the frozen Base value of $18.56.
The 2025 20-F states management compensation includes fixed pay, profit sharing and long-term RSU awards, with the majority intended to be delivered as share-based compensation.
David Vélez retained controlling Class B voting power through a dual-class structure, materially limiting minority shareholder influence.
Nu converted Mexico into a full bank, is evolving the Brazil license structure, and has deployed NuFormer across multiple underwriting portfolios and customer service.
Management reorganized reporting lines in 2025, with the founder resuming direct command and product/market responsibilities reallocated across COO, Brazil CEO and technology leadership.

counterevidence: Founder voting control can override minority preferences.
The buyback began only recently and competes with high-return growth uses of capital.
International expansion adds execution and regulatory complexity.
Credit-cycle outcomes can reveal allocation errors with a lag.
unknowns: Explicit internal hurdle rates by country/product.
Long-run dilution from RSUs after buyback offsets.
Board challenge process under founder voting control.
falsifiers: Buybacks continue above intrinsic value while capital buffers weaken.
Credit or international expansion persistently earns below the cost of equity.
Material accounting, control or governance failures emerge.

hard_veto_flags.veto: 경영진 정직성 또는 회계 신뢰성 훼손
hard_veto_flags.rationale: Audited/reviewed filings and compensation disclosures show no current accounting-integrity impairment. Founder control is a governance discount, not evidence of dishonesty.

subscores.rationale: Average H1 repurchase price was about 0.663x the frozen Base value, directly mapping to the <0.8 observable row. Growth reinvestment also remains high-return.
Reporting quality and incentive alignment are good, but dominant founder voting control materially reduces governance checks and prevents a 75-90 score.
Nu has repeatedly adapted product, organizational and regulatory structures across Brazil, Mexico and Colombia while deploying AI into core underwriting and service.

uncertainties.rationale: The buyback is recent and should be judged against future capital needs.
Dual-class founder control is structurally significant despite no integrity red flag.
Execution evidence across markets and products is strong.
